scholarships.title: The Inlaks Fellowship for Social Engagement
scholarships.degree: Not a degree programme (open to Indian bachelor's-degree holders and early to mid-career professionals)

eligibility: The applicant must be an Indian citizen currently residing in India.
The applicant must be born on or after 1st January 1991.
The applicant must be a graduate (hold a Bachelor's degree) from a recognised institute/university in India.
In the absence of a Bachelor's degree, they must carry at least three years of relevant work experience.
Those enrolled in academic studies/PhD for the duration of the fellowship are NOT eligible to apply.
Applicants proposing to work on art installations, photo books etc. are not eligible to apply for this fellowship.
existing.eligibility_summary: Indian citizens residing in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, who are graduates of a recognised Indian institution or have at least three years of relevant work experience, and who are not enrolled in academic study or a PhD for the fellowship period.
benefits: Monthly fellowship stipend for two years, at INR 45,000 / 35,000 / 25,000 per month depending on whether the fellow is living and working in an 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' category area (final amount at the Foundation's discretion)
No tuition, travel, health insurance or equipment costs are listed as covered by the award on the published pages
coverage: Monthly fellowship stipend for two years, at INR 45,000 / 35,000 / 25,000 per month depending on whether the fellow is living and working in an 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' category area (final amount at the Foundation's discretion)
No tuition, travel, health insurance or equipment costs are listed as covered by the award on the published pages
requirements: Complete all questions in the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS)
Enter name, address and latest contact information correctly
For the 'Topic of your project' field, describe the fellowship activity in a few lines so that it correctly represents the nature of the project
Statement of purpose and work plan must be completed in the Foundation's own format and uploaded as PDF only
Your Statement of purpose and work plan must not exceed 1000 words each
The statement of purpose must outline the applicant's personal and professional trajectory very briefly, and the motivation for taking up the project and how it contributes to social change

The work plan must include a title of the proposed work with a concise description of the work or research planned during the fellowship, the expected outcomes, and in detail the manner in which the project will be undertaken with a clear timeline for 2 years
Two letters are required: a Mentor endorsement letter and a Recommendation letter

The Mentor endorsement letter must include a brief description of the mentor's work experience, the mentor's contact details (email and official address), a statement of why the mentor endorses the applicant's work plan, a statement that the mentor agrees to supervise the applicant's work during the fellowship, willingness to review and comment on quarterly and annual progress reports, and willingness to hold periodic meetings with the Foundation so it can assess the fellow's progress

The Letter of Recommendation must elaborate the nature of engagement with the applicant (in what capacity they engaged with the applicant) and the reason why the referee would like to recommend the applicant and the work plan

The Recommendation letter must be from a person who has supervised the applicant's work for at least 6 months; this cannot be the same person as the mentor. For fresh graduates, an academic letter of recommendation is acceptable
The mentor or referee cannot be someone who is currently an Inlaks Fellow or currently being supported by Inlaks under any other opportunity
Please ensure that both the Mentor and Referee letters are also submitted by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm
documents: Statement of purpose and work plan, in the Foundation's supplied format, uploaded as PDF only, 1000 words each maximum
Mentor endorsement letter, uploaded by the mentor through the link emailed to them
Letter of Recommendation, uploaded by the referee through the link emailed to them
Proof of age and citizenship (referenced in the published instructions for entering the Date of Birth field)
application_method: Click 'Apply Now' on the fellowship page to reach the Foundation's Online Application System (OAS), hosted on Submittable
Enter personal details; for Date of Birth scroll the calendar or type it exactly as shown on the proof of age and citizenship you upload
Describe the fellowship activity in the 'Topic of your project' field in a few lines
Download the Foundation's statement of purpose and work plan format, complete it and upload it as a PDF
Enter the mentor's email address in the Mentor Endorsement field and submit; the mentor then receives a link by email to upload their Letter of Endorsement
Enter the referee's email address in the recommendation field and submit; the referee then receives a link by email to upload their Letter of Recommendation

Note that the field text may show 'Enter the email address of the person you'd like to serve as a reference' by default even in the Mentor Endorsement section, so the applicant's mentor's email address must be entered there
Ensure both the mentor and referee letters are uploaded by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm, even before the applicant makes a final submission
existing.selection_notes: The selection procedure comprises two rounds: a desk-review of applications, followed by an online interview of the shortlisted applicants by a selection committee.
existing.best_fit: Indian citizens residing in India, born on or after 1 January 1991, who hold a bachelor's degree from a recognised Indian institution (or have at least three years of relevant work experience) and want two years to do self-directed research, cause lawyering, grassroots journalism, community-rights, public-health or ecological work.
existing.notes: This is a stipend for self-directed work, not money towards a degree: the published pages list no tuition, travel, insurance or project-cost coverage, so applicants must budget their own project costs. The fellowship is only to support individual learning and not for any organisational work. Applicants proposing to work on art installations or photo books are not eligible for this fellowship and are directed to the Inlaks Fine Arts Award instead. The stipend is a range and the final amount is at the Foundation's discretion. Fellows are subject to a six-month probation period and quarterly and annual reviews, and must attend three Foundation-hosted workshops.
existing.duration: Two years, with a six-month probation period and quarterly and annual review of the Fellow's work
existing.application_period: Applications open for the 2027 cohort (opening date not published on the page); closing 15 November 2026, 11:59pm IST. Shortlisted candidates announced by the last week of February 2027, final interview within a fortnight, final fellows announced by the last week of March, fellows expected to begin work from 1 May 2027
existing.deadline_display: Applications for the fellowship can be submitted latest by 15th November 2026 by 11.59 PM IST; both the Mentor and Referee letters must also be submitted by 15th November 2026, 11:59pm
